newsitem.title: ITALY: Telecom Italia core investors ready by end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia core investors ready by end-Sept.

text.p: The group of investors that will form a core of stable shareholders at Italian telecoms operator Telecom Italia SpA
should be in place by the end of September, the Treasury said in a statement on Wednesday.
The statement added that the general placement of Telecom shares aimed at institutional and retail investors was set for the second half of October.

The state's flotation of its 44 percent stake in Telecom Italia is likely to be one of the largest disposals the world will see this year and has been dubbed in Italy as "the mother of all privatisations."
The Treasury said the sale would take place in two phases: first the core of shareholders will be selected, then the remaining stock will be offered to institutions and the general public.

No single company or investor will be able to hold more than three percent and Italian newspapers have speculated that around 15 percent of Telecom stock will be placed in the hands of the core investors.

The Treasury statement said that its two advisors for the sale, Morgan Stanley and Italian merchant bank Mediobanca, will shortly embark on a survey to gauge market interest in the placement. It added that some 100 investors seen as potential core shareholders had already been contacted.
Due diligence of companies that show an interest in joining the inner elite will start after September 2.
"It is expected that the formation of the stable shareholder group will be completed by the end of September," the Treasury statement said.

Among firms believed to be considering joining the stable core are the Agnelli family holding IFIL, banking group Istituto San Paolo di Torino, Germany's Mannesmann and U.S. telecommunications group AT&T.
Telecom Italia is the world's sixth largest telephone operator by number of subscribers and controls Europe's biggest mobile phone firm, Telecom Italia Mobile.
